Header:
Date: 2026-06-19
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Liu (Redwood AE), Carlos Mendes (Redwood SE), Nora Patel (Redwood CSM); Mark Reynolds (Peregrine Head of Procurement), Aisha Khan (Peregrine Legal), Dr. Lena Ortiz (CTO), Samir Gupta (IT Security), Olivia Park (Project Manager)

Summary (auto):
Redwood and Peregrine reviewed MSA/DPA redlines, SLA expectations, and onboarding timeline. Customer expressed concerns about data residency, SOC2 and KMS integration. Redwood agreed to run a performance benchmark on dedicated capacity and to provide redlined contracts and an onboarding checklist. Next steps and owners captured at end.

Topics: MSA redlines, DPA / Data residency, SLAs (p99 latency), Pricing approvals, Dedicated vs Hosted, KMS integration, Onboarding timeline

Action items: see metadata list above

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Jamie (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you all making time. We're going to run through the MSA and DPA redlines, SLA ask, and then talk onboarding and pricing approvals. Quick intro from our side — I'm Jamie, AE, and with me is Carlos our SE and Nora who will own onboarding.
[00:00:15] Mark (Peregrine): Thanks, Jamie. On our side I'm Mark Reynolds, procurement lead, Aisha's here from legal, Lena from tech, Samir for security and Olivia for PM.
[00:00:24] Jamie: Great, quick agenda — 1) legal redlines on MSA/DPA, 2) SLA specifics and what we can guarantee (p50/p95/p99), 3) pricing / procurement cadence, 4) onboarding steps. Sound OK?
[00:00:35] Aisha (Legal): Yep good. We already sent an initial redline, want to walk through the major points. Also we have a few non-negotiables on data residency and breach notification windows.
[00:00:45] Carlos (Redwood SE): Quick note — some of our product names might be slightly different in the doc, e.g., Redwood Dedicated we sometimes refer to as "Dedicated Capacity" in the contract. Sorry if that caused confusion.
[00:00:55] Lena (CTO): Noted. We care most about where the data sits and key management — we want customer-managed KMS in the VPC option.
[00:01:10] Samir (Security): Also SOC 2 Type II, ISO, and audit logs retention — what's default retention and can we increase it?
[00:01:20] Jamie: We are SOC 2 Type II — we can provide the report during diligence. Logs retention is configurable as an add-on, default 90 days but we can extend to 12 months with the compliance package. I'll put that in the next steps.
[00:01:35] Mark: Aisha flagged the liability cap, indemnity, and the DPA's data processing clauses are tighter than our standard. We're a healthcare-adjacent firm, some PHI-ish PII concerns — though we will push to avoid true PHI, we still need guarantees.
[00:01:50] Aisha: Yes please, and timelines on breach notifications — 72 hours is our policy. Can you commit?
[00:01:58] Jamie: Our standard is 72 hours for confirmed breaches with an initial notification within 24 hours for incidents we suspect may involve customer data, but legal can get into exact wording. We'll send a redline that maps to that.
[00:02:12] [00:02:15] Speaker 1: (mumble) can I ask about on prem — sorry — 
[00:02:18] Lena: On-prem question — we may need a private deployment option, VPC is likely, but in the worst case we might need an air-gapped install for a subset of sensitive workloads. Is that supported?
[00:02:32] Carlos: Short answer, yes. Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem packages with an optional air-gapped install. There's a bit of engineering lead time — usually 6-8 weeks depending on the scope. For hybrid setups we can route less sensitive inference to hosted and sensitive to Private.
[00:02:46] Samir: And does Private allow customer KMS, HSM integrations?
[00:02:50] Carlos: Yes, customer-managed KMS/HSM is supported for Private and for Dedicated we have KMS integrations as well. There might be a few keys management caveats for streaming logs, but we can capture that detail in the DPA addendum.
[00:03:05] Jamie: On SLAs — per our standard offer, hosted customers get a best-effort 99.9% availability with latency SLOs per model; Dedicated has stronger SLOs and SLA credits. We're happy to align on p99 latency targets for your key routes as part of the Dedicated contract.
[00:03:22] Mark: We'd like explicit p99 under 400ms for our low-latency routing for clinician-facing UI — that's critical. How realistic is that?
[00:03:30] Carlos: Depends on model size and sequence length. For our optimized quantized weights on Dedicated with continuous batching tuned for short requests we can hit ~200-350ms p99 on 8-16 token responses, but that assumes dedicated GPUs and the right kernel selection. We'll run a benchmark against your sample prompt set to validate.
[00:03:49] Lena: Good, we'll share a sample prompt set. We have some longer ones too for batch jobs but UI needs the low-latency path.
[00:03:57] [00:04:00] Olivia (PM): Timeline wise procurement wants to get procurement sign-off by end of month, budgeting needs final pricing by next Wednesday.
[00:04:08] Jamie: Understood. On pricing — we quoted hosted per-token rates in the spreadsheet you saw; Dedicated pricing is commit-based with options for burst. If procurement needs an approval pack, I can send a 1-pager showing TCO comparison hosted vs dedicated vs private with expected monthly cost at your 50k/day traffic profile.
[00:04:25] Mark: That would help — please include amortized committed-discount scenarios.
[00:04:30] Jamie: Will do. Also note there is a one-time onboarding fee for Private deployments and a slightly higher enterprise support tier for SLA-backed Dedicated.
[00:04:40] Aisha: On indemnity and liability cap — we are asking for the cap to be raised for security incidents and to exclude data-subject damages from the cap. Is that something you'll consider?
[00:04:52] Jamie: We typically have a balanced approach. We can discuss carve-outs for willful misconduct and gross negligence, but unlimited liability is hard. We can propose higher caps for security incidents and carve-outs for certain data breach classes. I'll flag this for legal escalation and include suggested language in the redline.
[00:05:08] [00:05:12] Speaker 2 (muffled): so the DPA, retention periods?
[00:05:14] Nora (CSM): For onboarding, retention, and access controls — we maintain audit logs, token-level usage, and you can configure retention; for the compliance pack we provide extended retention and dedicated retention buckets. I'll share the onboarding checklist and links to the docs in the next email.
[00:05:28] Samir: Re: audit logs — can logs be exported to our SIEM in near real-time? We use Splunk.
[00:05:33] Carlos: Yes, we have log hooks and can stream to customer SIEM via secure syslog or S3 ingestion. There is a small integration lead but it's standard. We'll include doc links.
[00:05:42] Lena: For the benchmark, also include cold-start latency and how KV cache prefixing affects p99 for chat flows. We've seen big differences when caching is warm.
[00:05:52] Carlos: Good call — we'll measure both cold and warm cache scenarios and show per-route token efficiency, cost per 1k tokens, and p99 tail.
[00:05:59] Mark: Procurement also asked about subcontractors and where code runs — e.g., cloud providers, geographic regions. We need a list of providers and data centers.
[00:06:08] Jamie: We can provide a list of our hosting regions and major cloud providers used for hosting; for Private you control the region. We'll include that in the compliance packet and the regional addendum.
[00:06:16] Aisha: SSO and RBAC — we need SAML, SCIM provisioning, and role-based access. Also MFA for all user roles.
[00:06:24] Nora: We support SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and granular RBAC. MFA can be enforced through your IdP. I'll attach the admin guide.
[00:06:32] [00:06:35] Speaker 1: any questions on pricing tiers?
[00:06:37] Mark: How do overage fees work for Dedicated bursts? We want predictable monthly costs.
[00:06:42] Jamie: Dedicated is commit-based — you get a committed monthly throughput and discounted token pricing. Burst is allowed up to a threshold and billed at a pre-agreed burst rate; we can add a cap to prevent runaway charges. We'll include a sample contract clause.
[00:06:55] Lena: For private, do you require network egress rules or do you support our firewall policies?
[00:07:01] Carlos: We can work with your firewall; Private often runs in your VPC with customer-managed networking. There is a support matrix for inbound/outbound rules we'll share.
[00:07:10] Aisha: Any standard exceptions in the MSA around change-in-law or export controls? We need to see those.
[00:07:15] Jamie: Yes there are standard clauses; we'll map them out in the redline.
[00:07:20] [00:07:24] Olivia: Procurement timeline: If we get pricing and redlines by next Wednesday we can aim to sign in two weeks. Is that realistic?
[00:07:31] Jamie: Yes, that's feasible. We need legal alignment on both sides but our goal is to have a signed MSA and DPA in 2 weeks if reviews go smoothly.
[00:07:38] Samir: On the technical side, we will require a short security assessment — ideally a 1-week questionnaire and an optional scan. Do you have a standard security questionnaire?
[00:07:45] Carlos: We do — I'll send our security questionnaire and a SOC 2 report. We also support a whitebox or blackbox scan under NDA for Private deployments.
[00:07:55] [00:08:00] Jamie: Alright, quick recap so everyone's on the same page — Redwood to: 1) send redlined MSA & DPA with suggested language for liability and breach timelines (Jamie); 2) run SLA/latency bench with your sample prompts (Carlos); 3) share onboarding checklist, admin guide for SSO/RBAC, and compliance packet including SOC2 (Nora); 4) Peregrine legal to return redlines (Aisha) and procurement to confirm pricing approval timeline (Mark/Olivia).
[00:08:20] Aisha: One more thing — data residency: we need EU-only for a subset of data. Can that be scoped per tenant?
[00:08:27] Carlos: Yes, we can scope region by tenant and route requests to EU regions only. We'll document that in the DPA addendum.
[00:08:36] Mark: Great. Also, can you include a sample SLA credit calculation so procurement can evaluate financial impact?
[00:08:42] Jamie: Absolutely, we'll include the SLA credits table and an example calculation.
[00:08:48] [00:09:00] Speaker 2: (laughter) cool, thanks everyone.
[00:09:05] Nora: I'll follow up after the call with a consolidated email that includes links to the contract, pricing spreadsheet, SOC2, and onboarding docs.
[00:09:12] Olivia: Perfect. If we get those items we can move to internal approvals.
[00:09:18] Jamie: Thanks all — we'll target delivering the redline and benchmark plan by the dates we discussed. Any final questions?
[00:09:25] Lena: No, that's it for me.
[00:09:27] Aisha: I'm good.
[00:09:29] Mark: Thanks everyone.
[00:09:32] Jamie: Alright, we'll wrap. Thanks all.

Meeting end: 15:58 UTC
